(a) 
Passenger Automobiles.—

        (1) 
In general.—
Subparagraph (A) of section 4961(a)(2) (relating to tax on passenger automobiles, etc.) is amended to read as follows:


“(A) 

Articles enumerated in subparagraph (B) are taxable at whichever of the following rates is applicable:


 
  “If the article is sold—
  The tax rate is—



 
  Before January 1, 1970
  7 percent
 
 
  During 1970
  5 percent
 
 
  During 1971
  3 percent
 
 
  During 1972
  1 percent
 


The tax imposed by this subsection shall not apply with respect to articles enumerated in subparagraph (B) which are sold by the manufacturer, producer, or importer after December 31, 1972.”




 
        (2) 
Conforming amendment.—
Sect ion 6412(a)(1) (relating to floor stocks refunds on passenger automobiles, etc.) is amended by striking out “May 1, 1968, or January 1, 1969,” and inserting in lieu thereof “January 1, 1970, January 1, 1971, January 1, 1972, or January 1, 1973,”.
  
    (b) 
Communications Services.—

        (1) 
Continuation of tax.—Paragraph (2) of section 4251(a) (relating to tax on certain communications services) is amended to read as follows:


“(2) 
The rate of tax referred to in paragraph (1) is as follows:


 
  “Amounts paid pursuant to bills first redered—
  Percent—



 
  Before January 1, 1970
  10 
 
 
  During 1970
  5 
 
 
  During 1971
  3 
 
 
  During 1972 
  1.”
 






 
        (2) 
Conforming amendments.—
Subsection (b) of section4251 (relating to termination of tax) is amended by striking out “January 1, 1969” and inserting in lieu thereof “January 1, 1973”, and subsection (c) of section 4251 is amended to read as follows:


“(c) 
Special Rule.—
For purposes of subsections (a) and (b), in the case of communications services rendered before November 1 of a calendar year for which a bill has not been rendered before the close of such year, a bill shall be treated as having been first rendered on December 31 of such year.”



 
        (3) 
Repeal of subchafter b of chapter 33.—Effective with respect to amounts paid pursuant to bills first rendered on or after January 1, 1973, subchapter B of chapter 33 (relating to the tax on communications) is repealed. For purposes of the preceding sentence, in the case of communications services rendered before November 1, 1972, for which a bill has not been rendered before January 1, 1973, a bill shall be treated as having been first rendered on December 31, 1972. Effective January 1, 1973, the table of subchapters for chapter 33 is amended by striking out the item relating to such subchapter B.
  
    (c) 
Effective Date.—
The amendments made by this section shall take effect as of April 30, 1968.

fable.w: This section only amends excise tax rates and termination dates for passenger automobiles and communications services, with conforming amendments and an effective date. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to comment on or challenge any federal decision. The only possible lure is the reference to manufacturers, producers, and importers, but they appear solely as taxpayers, not as participants in a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section amends tax code provisions to set specific tax rates and effective dates for passenger automobiles and communications services. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as manufacturers or service providers) before the government makes a decision. The mention of manufacturers and importers is solely in the context of who is subject to the tax, not who participates in the policy-making process.
qwen_block.s: The tax imposed by this subsection shall not apply with respect to articles enumerated in subparagraph (B) which are sold by the manufacturer, producer, or importer after December 31, 1972.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "manufacturer, producer, or importer" and "communications services," it involves outside parties. However, the text only defines tax rates and effective dates for these entities; it does not require them to consult with the government, nor does it grant them a role in the decision-making process. The interaction is purely regulatory (paying taxes), not participatory.

opus.w: This section only amends tax rate schedules, phase-out dates and conforming references for the automobile and communications excise taxes. The mention of floor stocks refunds is a mechanism for taxpayers to claim money back, which is like applying for a benefit. It is not outside parties taking part in a federal decision. Nothing here involves consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies or a right to sue.
opus.b: 1. **Analysis:** This section changes excise tax rates on passenger automobiles and communications services, sets dates when those taxes phase out, and repeals one subchapter. A reader might latch onto the mention of "floor stocks refunds." That fails the test: claiming a tax refund is like applying for a benefit, and nothing in the section has anyone outside the federal government consult on a federal decision. There's no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends tax rates and effective dates for passenger automobiles and communications services. It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or companies) before the government makes a decision. The changes are mandated by statute without a participatory process.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the tax rates affect the general public or companies, so their "participation" is implied. However, the definition requires a specific mechanism for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties *before* a decision is made. This section merely sets statutory tax rates and effective dates; it does not invite comments, hearings, or advisory input from the public or industry.
